Ontology Quality: visual reference

Companion specimen for specs/quality/README.md, which owns the QLY requirement prefix. Every figure names the requirements it demonstrates.

This is a picture, not a specification. Where this file and README.md disagree, README.md wins and this file is the defect. No screenshot of this surface exists, because the pane has never run in the Axiom application. These figures carry that load instead.

A. The eight scan states

The single easiest thing to get wrong in this pane is letting a scan that was canceled, failed, stale, or run with no checks enabled read as a clean bill of health. Each of the eight states therefore has its own presentation, and four of them say in words that they are not a clean result.

Demonstrates QLY-80 through QLY-85, QLY-19, QLY-88.

B. The vocabulary census

A check that tests how a vocabulary is used is withdrawn when that vocabulary is absent from the loaded ontology. It is not listed, not counted, not given a group chip, and not reported as passing. A check that tests for something missing is never gated, because the thing it looks for is absent by definition.

Demonstrates QLY-66 through QLY-74, QLY-40, QLY-44.

The two sides of the gate, side by side. The left column is withdrawn by the census; the right column is never gated, because a rule that fires on absence cannot require the absent thing to be present. Gating the license rule on Dublin Core would guarantee it never fires on the ontologies that most need it. QLY-67, QLY-69

RuleTestsCensusDisposition
naming.skos.preflabel.cardinality How SKOS labels are used skos absent Withdrawn. Not listed, not counted, no coverage row.
retired.reference How retirement is annotated owl:deprecated absent Withdrawn, taking its group with it.
completeness.label.missing Whether a label is absent not gated Runs. 1,284 findings.
meta.license.missing Whether a license is absent not gated Runs, although Dublin Core is absent. That absence is the finding.

C. Findings grouped by rule

Thousands of findings cannot be a flat list. Each rule gets a band carrying its own severity, identifier and count. The page window runs over the findings actually listed, so a collapsed rule contributes nothing to the pager.

Demonstrates QLY-94, QLY-96, QLY-97, QLY-103 through QLY-109.

D. The finding detail

Nine fields in a fixed order. The one that earns its place is Reading: it names what the application currently displays, which is why a missing label is invisible in ordinary browsing and why the rule must read statements rather than the display fallback.

Demonstrates QLY-110 through QLY-114, QLY-158, QLY-161.

E. Coverage with denominators

A percentage with an unstated denominator is a false claim, and 98% complete is the exact shape of that claim. Every row carries its applicable count in the same row as its percentage, and not applicable is presented as a different fact from zero missing.

Demonstrates QLY-117 through QLY-125, QLY-36, QLY-38.

F. Exceptions

An exception is a review decision, not an assertion about the world, so it is stored in workbench preferences outside the ontology RDF. Its key includes a fingerprint of the finding's evidence and policy, which is what forces a re-review when either changes.

Demonstrates QLY-126 through QLY-133.

StepBehaviourRequirement
1. Record The reviewer supplies a reason. A reason is required, not optional. QLY-126
2. Store Written to workbench preferences, outside the ontology RDF. QLY-127
3. Key ontology identity · exact entity · rule · fingerprint of the evidence and policy QLY-128
4. Effect The finding leaves its severity count and enters the suppressed count. The two are never added together. QLY-132, QLY-119
5. Invalidate Changed evidence or changed policy forces the finding to be reviewed again. The old decision does not carry over to different data. QLY-129
6. Remove Through Show suppressed findings or through Recorded exceptions. QLY-130
7. Persist Survives application restarts and source reloads. QLY-131

G. Reviewed label additions

This is the one write path in scope, and it is the workflow quality.html is missing entirely. The prototype renders Would add as a read only preview on the belief that repair was future scope; docs/ontology-quality.md describes it as built and names its tests. The prototype is the defect.

Demonstrates QLY-141 through QLY-157. The divergence is QLY-12 and Appendix B.1 row 1.

H. The four presentations, live

Every pane below is resizable from its bottom right corner. Drag one across 600 wide or 400 tall and it re-tiers off its own rectangle, not the window. The thresholds come from docs/adaptive-pane-ux.md; no number here was invented.

Demonstrates QLY-168 through QLY-175. Try it: narrow the first pane and watch the kind and IRI fold into the name cell rather than disappear.

I. Severity without colour

Three distinct glyph shapes, each paired with its word. Severity survives greyscale, colour blindness and a monochrome print.

Demonstrates QLY-56, QLY-179, QLY-51.

One sentence carries more weight than the glyphs. QLY-51 requires the surface to state that a configured project violation is not automatically an RDF or OWL standards violation. Without it, the word Violation reads as a claim about correctness that a review tool is not entitled to make.

J. Dark theme, audited independently

Dark is authored as its own token block measured against #1e1e1e, not derived by inverting light. The status colours in particular are different hues, not the same hues flipped.

Demonstrates QLY-177, QLY-178, QLY-27.

K. What the prototype gets wrong

quality.html diverges from this specification in thirteen places. The prototype is the defect in every one. The full table with requirement references is Appendix B.1 of README.md; the four that change behaviour rather than coverage are below.

#DivergenceRequirementSeverity
1 The correction preview is read only. No candidate selection, no predicate or language editing, no preview token, no apply, no undo. The whole workflow of exhibit G is absent, on the belief that repair was future scope. QLY-12, QLY-141 to QLY-157 Blocking. A regression against built behaviour.
2 Severity is a fixed property of each rule and cannot be reassigned or disabled per rule. QLY-54, QLY-55 High
3 Exceptions are an in memory reason string: no ontology identity, no evidence and policy fingerprint, no re-review on change, no Recorded exceptions view, no persistence. QLY-126 to QLY-133 High
4 A seventh group named SKOS integrity exists. The documented six groups contain no SKOS group; the rule belongs in naming. QLY-10, QLY-46 Medium

Two of these are my errors, not the implementer's. Row 1 exists because the prototype was built from issue 42 before docs/ontology-quality.md was read, and the issue calls repair future scope while the doc describes it as built and names its tests. Row 4 exists for the same reason: the issue names nine check groups and the doc names six, and the six do not include SKOS.

Ontology Quality visual reference. Companion to specs/quality/README.md, which owns the QLY prefix and wins every disagreement with this file.

Self contained: no dependencies, no build step, no network requests. Tokens are carried unchanged from quality.html, which carries them from index.html and find.html. Light and dark are independent blocks, each audited on its own.

No em dashes and no en dashes appear in this file, per a standing instruction. Separators are the middot, the colon and the period.
